Jonathan S. "JKT" Kreiss-Tomkins

Registered Democrat / Nonpartisan candidate for Governor / Lieutenant Governor, Alaska · Open seat

Former state representative; business owner

Jonathan S. "JKT" Kreiss-Tomkins is a Democrat from Sitka who served in the Alaska House of Representatives from 2013 to 2023. He is running for governor with Zac Johnson as his running mate to succeed term-limited Gov. Mike Dunleavy. He advanced from the August 18, 2026 nonpartisan top-four primary to the ranked-choice general election.

Where Kreiss-Tomkins stands

Education funding
Supports fully funding and forward-funding public schools. Says the current governor has defunded schools for nearly a decade. Supports getting cell phones out of classrooms.
School choice
Opposes a constitutional amendment to have public education funding follow the child. Says he supports freedom of education, but not publicly funded freedom of education.
Permanent Fund
Supports amending the state constitution to restrict Permanent Fund spending and prevent overspending of the fund.
Permanent Fund Dividend
Opposes a $4,000 dividend this year, arguing it would drain the fund within decades. Supports a smaller dividend he says is sustainable.
Fisheries
Calls for a "fish first" governor: reducing bycatch, putting Alaskans rather than Lower 48 trawl interests in charge of fisheries, and stopping the Pebble Mine to protect salmon habitat.
Health care
Supports protecting Medicaid expansion and expanding telehealth.
Energy and cost of living
Proposes lowering electric bills by making utilities cooperate and by building renewable energy. Supports cutting red tape to build more homes and easing regulations on new childcare providers.

Background

  • Alaska State Representative, District 35, 2013–2023
  • Former state representative and business owner (self-reported occupation)
  • Sitka High School; attended Yale College, left without a degree
  • Born in Sitka in 1989; lived in Sitka until 2024 and in Anchorage since 2025
  • Eagle Scout
